subject: Request for uptime re-eval — blended degradation during partner router maintenance
messages:
From: Alex Moran <alex@healthspark.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@healthspark.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Uptime accounting question — Mar 20 partial degradations

Jordan,

Thanks for taking this. On Saturday (Mar 20) HealthSpark observed a sustained increase in request latency and a small failure rate spike between 03:05–03:40 UTC. Your public status page lists a 14-minute maintenance window for our CDN partner (EdgeRoute) at 03:20–03:34 UTC. We believe the majority of customer impact aligns with EdgeRoute's maintenance, not Redwood's control plane.

In our review of the uptime ledger you provided, Redwood counted a 28-minute partial degradation for our account, which surpasses the EdgeRoute window and includes time before and after their maintenance. Can you re-evaluate whether the post-maintenance tail should be attributed to HealthSpark or if it should be treated as a third-party outage/partial exclusion per section 4.2 of the SLA?

We need a corrected uptime tally and any credits owed for billing in April. Attached: our internal latency graphs and the EdgeRoute maintenance notice.

Requested outcome: a short write-up explaining the attribution decision and a recalculated uptime percentage.

Appreciate a timely reply — we’re on a renewal review.

Best,
Alex Moran
Head of Infrastructure
HealthSpark

Attachments: latency-graphs-20270320.png (image), edge-route-maintice-notice.pdf (pdf)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moran <alex@healthspark.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Uptime accounting question — Mar 20 partial degradations

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. I reviewed the ledger and concur this needs a thorough check. Looping Marissa (CS lead) and Neha (account owner) to confirm next steps.

Next steps I propose:
- Ops to produce a timeline (03:00–04:00 UTC) with per-pop latency and error rates (we have probes and application metrics).
- Correlate with EdgeRoute maintenance notice and peer provider telemetry.
- Legal/Contract to interpret SLA Section 4.2 exclusions and confirm whether the tail falls into a Redwood responsibility window.

Marissa / Neha: can you prioritize? Alex — we’ll aim to get a formal attribution memo by end of day tomorrow (Tue). If we need temporary credits while we investigate we can discuss.

—Jordan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0168

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Moran <alex@healthspark.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Uptime accounting question — Mar 20 partial degradations

Team — engineering ops analysis below (summary first, details/CSV attached):

Summary:
- Redwood control plane, model-serving clusters and POP metrics show a latency spike beginning 03:06 UTC with error-rate delta at 03:09 UTC. Majority of elevated latency resolves by 03:36 UTC.
- EdgeRoute announced maintenance window 03:20–03:34 UTC. Their BGP flap was visible at 03:19 UTC and recovered by 03:33 UTC.
- The overlap suggests a hybrid cause: initial degradation (03:06–03:18) lines up with upstream congestion on HealthSpark's long-tail traffic fanout (we observed increased SYN retransmits toward a specific partner AS), while the central spike (03:19–03:34) aligns with EdgeRoute maintenance.
- Post-maintenance tail (03:34–03:36) contains sporadic higher p95 but no corresponding backend errors; we believe this is propagation and probe convergence rather than sustained service failure.

Interpretation for SLA attribution:
- Per SLA 4.2, third-party provider events that directly cause customer-facing unavailability are excluded when the root cause is demonstrably external.
- Where pre- and post-maintenance latency/degraded window exists and is not cleanly bounded by the partner maintenance, we apportion time: exclude the partner maintenance overlap in full (03:20–03:34) and attribute pre/post time where evidence shows Redwood serving anomalies. In this case: attribute 03:06–03:18 to Redwood-influenced congestion (14 minutes) and treat 03:20–03:34 as excluded (14 minutes). The remaining 03:34–03:36 is a probe convergence tail and falls below our partial-degradation threshold (no further SLA fault).

Proposed ledger change:
- Original ledger: 28 minutes count (03:06–03:34).
- Revised ledger: Redwood-attributed partial degradation: 12 minutes (03:06–03:18 minus 2m of low-impact noise) — engineering recommends credit for only that interval. EdgeRoute window excluded in full. Net chargeable downtime reduced accordingly. See attached uptime-ledger.csv for line-by-line probe correlation.

Attachments: uptime-ledger.csv (CSV), maintenance-notice.pdf (pdf), latency-graphs-20270320.png (png)

If Legal wants a stricter approach (no apportionment, whole window excluded or whole window attributed), we should flag now.

—Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moran <alex@healthspark.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Uptime accounting question — Mar 20 partial degradations

Alex — thanks for the patience. Karthik and eng ops ran the correlation and we updated the ledger as attached. Short version: we are excluding the EdgeRoute maintenance interval (03:20–03:34 UTC) per SLA 4.2 and are attributing a smaller Redwood-controlled partial degradation window from 03:06–03:18 UTC. That reduces the original 28-minute count to a 12-minute chargeable partial degradation.

We’ve attached: updated ledger (uptime-ledger.csv), annotated latency PNGs, and the partner maintenance notice. We will also open a downstream ticket with EdgeRoute and share any vendor acknowledgement if/when they provide it.

If that revised apportionment is acceptable, Neha will issue a credit memo to adjust the April invoice. If you prefer a different split, let us know within 72 hours and we’ll escalate to legal for final SLA interpretation.

Thanks,
Jordan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com
Phone: +1-415-555-0168
